newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares make bullish start to week.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares make bullish start to week.

text.p: Shares remained strong in active trading on the Nigerian stock market on Monday, consolidating earlier gains, traders said.
The all-share index moved up to 7729.29 from 7699.28 on Friday on positive movements recorded in most sectors.
Traders said investors were not deterred by soaring prices of popular shares which have risen sharply since January.

"Demand is particularly strong for food/beverages and petroleum stocks despite their astronomical prices," one trader said. "Buyers are creating the impression that their sources of funds are inexhaustive."
Monday's trading also saw conglomerate PZ strengthen by a one kobo at 23.11 naira after losing 5.45 naira since January 29.
The gain was attributed to speculators who felt it had touched the bottom and could now only appreciate.
But other conglomerates fell on excess supply. John Holt was down one kobo at 9.59 naira and SCOA closed two kobo lower at 2.18 naira.
Healthcare company Smithkline Beecham was also four kobo lower at 6.96 naira while Amicable Insurance dropped one kobo at 67 kobo.
Cadbury soared to 33.23 naira, up 33 kobo, Nigerian Bottling Company chalked up 20 kobo to close at 43.70 naira while Nestle finished 10 kobo up at 60.85 naira.
Dunlop, putting last week's one-day strike behind it, continued its comeback with a 20 kobo rise to 10.90 naira.
Unipetrol at 72.85 naira remained the market's dearest stock, adding 15 kobo. Total followed, 20 kobo higher at 70.20 naira.
